title_original: Mark Tildesley, production designer on James Bond, 2012 Olympics, dies aged 63
excerpt_original: Tildesley worked on films by Danny Boyle, Sam Mendes, Paul Thomas Anderson.

blocks.text: Acclaimed British production designer Mark Tildesley, who worked on the James Bond film series and with directors including Danny Boyle, Paul Thomas Anderson, Mike Leigh and Sam Mendes, has died aged 63.
Tildesley died on Tuesday, November 24 following a long illness.
He had over 40 production designer credits in a career spanning 35 years, which began with UK TV series and short films, before a first feature in 1995, Carl Prechezer’s Blue Juice .
Tildesley worked with many of the leading UK filmmakers of the 1990s and ’00s, including Michael Winterbottom on Wonderland and 24 Hour Party People .

He came to wide acclaim for creating a zombie-ravaged dystopian London for Danny Boyle’s 28 Days Later in 2002, including decorating the deserted streets of London shown in the film’s opening. He reunited with Boyle on 2004’s Millions , 2007’s Sunshine , 2013’s Trance and 2017’s T2: Trainspotting , as well as designing the set for Boyle’s 2011 stage production of Frankenstein .

His most renowned collaboration with Boyle was arguably Isles Of Wonder , the opening ceremony for the London 2012 Olympics. A spectacular show which paid tribute to the UK’s history and culture, it was widely praised as getting the Games off to an impressive start. Tildesley had begun working on ideas with Boyle two years prior to the event, and designed the four-hour show with Suttirat Anne Larlarb. It won numerous awards, including an Emmy for outstanding art direction for variety or nonfiction programming, for Tildesley, Larlarb and Boyle, and two nominations at the Bafta TV Craft awards.

Tildesley also received a Bafta Cymru award for best production design for Marc Evans’ 1997 House Of America ; and three Bifa nominations for best technical achievement, for 24 Hour Party People in 2002, Code 46 in 2004 and winning on the third occasion for Sunshine in 2007.
James Bond came calling at the end of the last decade, with Tildesley designing the production of Cary Fukunaga’s No Time To Die , Daniel Craig’s fifth and final outing as the British spy.

Other credits include Mike Leigh’s Happy-Go-Lucky , Lone Scherfig’s One Day , Ben Wheatley’s High-Rise , Ron Howard’s In The Heart Of The Sea , Paul Thomas Anderson’s Phantom Thread , Fernando Meirelles’ The Two Popes , Martin McDonagh’s The Banshees Of Inisherin , Joseph Kosinski’s F1: The Movie and Noah Baumbach’s Jay Kelly .

Tildesley also worked with Mendes on 2022’s Empire Of Light and most recently as production designer alongside Stefania Cella and Neal Callow for The Beatles – A Four Film Cinematic Event films, which are scheduled for release in April 2028.

”Mark was a one-off: gentle, funny, warm, mischievous, entirely original and extraordinarily gifted,” said Mendes in a statement shared with Screen . “My abiding memory of him is from Empire Of Light , flying down the Margate seafront on a motorised scooter, his technocolored scarf flapping in the wind, twinkling like a schoolboy playing hooky. A unique spirit and a wonderful artist. I am one of hundreds of people who are desperately sad that he is gone.”
The British Film Designers Guild (BFDG) awarded Tildesley on three occasions, for High-Rise , Empire Of Light and F1: The Movie .

“We are very sad to hear the news of Mark’s death,” said BFDG in a statement. “Besides being a well-respected and extremely talented production designer, he was a friend and colleague to many of our members and will be very much missed by everyone in the Industry who knew and worked with him.”
